Read the certificate off a result

Source: R/certificate.R
certificate.Rd

Every verb in this package that computes something returns a certificate with it, and each puts it where its own return value has room. A solve carries it in an attribute, so the result stays the matrix a matrix solve returns; the spectral verbs carry it in a field of their result; [verify()] returns one directly. This reads it off any of them.

Usage

certificate(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A result from [solve()], [eigs()], [svds()] or [verify()].

...

Unused.

Value

An object of class `linop_certificate`.

Details

A certificate belongs to a result and not to an operator. An operator on its own has nothing to certify: the claims a certificate makes are about a computation, and the one claim an operator can make alone is that it satisfies the contract, which is [verify()] and returns a certificate of its own.

A solve's attribute survives arithmetic on the solution and is dropped by indexing, `as.numeric()`, `c()` and the reductions. So the cost of [solve()] returning what a matrix solve returns is not that the certificate is easily lost: it is that `2 * x` still carries a certificate describing `x`.

Examples

A <- linop(diag(c(2, 3, 4)), properties = c(hermitian = TRUE,
                                            positive_definite = TRUE))
certificate(solve(A, c(2, 3, 4)))
certificate(eigs(A, k = 1))
certificate(verify(A))
